title: Billy Kersands and his wife Louisa
summary: Love describes Kersands' wife Louisa, who taught him his act and covered for him when he forgot his lines.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Billy Cassand had never been in Mississippi, you see. So they used his name on the car and he'd done that act on the stage, him and his wife. And he was forgetful, you know. His wife was named Louisa. She was a fine person. She was highly educated, you know. She learned him what he knew. He used to be a little shoeshine boy in Donisonville. And he had a big, funny looking mouth, you know. And he was really funny. He was apt and catching that foolishness. And she'd teach it to him. And towards last, they both was old. She was a good singer. And he used to forget his line, you know. But he had a word he used to say when he forget, you know. And she'd catch on to it. She'd know that word, you know. And you hear him say, Oh, Father, take my hand. I got full king. You know, that's telling her that he done forgot his line. And she'd just look around like that. The audience wouldn't notice it. And she'd just wake her mouth. And he could read her lips, you know. And he'd catch on, you know. He'd say, I know he's. He'd be kidding all the time. I know he's. I don't know what I'd do if it wasn't for you, you know. We could go and we was down in the pit, you know. That was a funny fellow.
You remember any of his jokes or anything?
